name: Twin Park
description: Digital twin scenes (park, city, workshop): inputs become ParkProgram IR, deterministic operators rebuild layered USD, and one package serves UE5, the web and the business systems.

tools.name: new-park
tools.description: Create a twin project from the template: park.json, catalog, viewer sources and contract docs. sceneClass picks park, city or workshop; the scaffold's facts follow it.

sceneClass.description: Which scene class this project is.

tools.name: ir-check
tools.description: Validate the project's ParkProgram IR: Q0 (manifest and stage present, scene class known) and Q1 self-consistency (ratios sum to 1, building counts agree, the tallest building's zone exists, conflicts carry questions). Run by the harness at run.prepare/checkpoint/finish; answers {block} to hold a moment back when the IR is inconsistent.

tools.name: gen-ir
tools.description: Write a consistent ParkProgram IR (ir.json) from a structured brief the agent supplies (sceneClass, brief J1, masterPlan J2, objects J3). Wraps every number into a provenance Field (source llm), derives the scene class and georef, runs Q1 self-consistency and reports any issues. Geometry tools read ir.json; the ir-check hook blocks delivery until Q1 passes.

program.description: The program: sceneClass, brief {siteAreaM2, far, coverage, maxHeightM, zones:[{id,landUse,ratio,buildings}], keyElements, assumptions, conflicts, questions}, masterPlan {redLine, setbackM, plots:[{id,ring,zoneId}], roads:[{id,points,widthM}], buildingOutlines:[{id,plotId,ring,heightM,floors,zoneId}]}, objects:[{id,element,kind?,params?,outputPath?}], environment?

tools.name: usd-info
tools.description: Inspect twin runtime readiness (the Python with pxr, the DWG converter, Blender for GLB export) and what to tell the user when one is missing. No account, no spending.

tools.name: gen-object
tools.description: Rebuild one object's .usdc layer from its IR task card (paradigm 1 parametric building, or paradigm 3 asset completion). Writes local-origin geometry with metric UVs, material slots and internal Q2 box QA; a failure degrades to a rule baseline and marks the object degraded.

kind.description: Which operator builds it; default from the element.

tools.name: gen-site
tools.description: Build the site layer (roads, kerbs, markings, landscape by difference, terrain) from the IR master plan's centerlines and plots.

tools.name: scatter
tools.description: Build the instancer layers (trees, shrubs, lamps, benches) from the IR scatter rules: one PointInstancer per element type, references to catalog prototypes, binding keys on devices.

tools.name: assemble
tools.description: Compose the delivery package: master_twin.usda with composition arcs and world transforms only, env and camera layers, twin_manifest.json, and the Q3 scene QA that blocks delivery.

tools.name: georeference
tools.description: Set the site's local frame: the CGCS2000 origin every layer is built around. Writes park.json and the IR environment.

tools.name: iot-bind
tools.description: Bind a device to a scene target: a prim, a device id, a property and the target it drives (position/rotation/scaling, material.emissive, visibility). Written to park.json for the web route and to twin_manifest.json's binding keys for UE5 and the business systems.

device.description: The device id in the IoT gateway.

target.description: What it drives, e.g. material.emissive, rotation.y, visibility.

tools.name: export-glb
tools.description: Export one object's USD layer to GLB for the web route, through local Blender's USD importer. The GLB keeps the object's local origin and tags.

object.description: The object id whose layer is exported.

workerTypes.description: Build one building or landmark layer from its IR task card.
Build roads, landscape and terrain from the master plan.
Place catalog instances (lamps, trees, furniture) as instancers.

skills.name: twin-ir
skills.summary: ParkProgram IR discipline: every field carries source, confidence and lock; only a person locks; conflicts resolve by source priority; changes land as diffs that rerun only affected objects.

skills.name: twin-elements
skills.summary: Engineering elements and the catalog: buildings, roads, lamps and devices are types with specs and instances, never hand-modelled meshes; one object one layer at local origin.

skills.name: twin-operators
skills.summary: The three operator paradigms (parametric buildings 60%, instancers 25%, asset completion 15%), their parameters and QA; you write parameters, operators write geometry.

skills.name: twin-input-adapters
skills.summary: How text, plan images, CAD, point clouds and orthophotos become IR and evidence only; scanned meshes are never deliverables.

skills.name: gis-alignment
skills.summary: CGCS2000 to the site's local ENU frame, GeoServer overlays, orthophoto registration; a twin that is not georeferenced is a diorama.

skills.name: iot-binding
skills.summary: Binding devices to scene targets: prim, device, property, target; one binding serves the web route and UE5's manifest keys; reverse control goes through a confirmation card.

skills.name: park-standards
skills.summary: Chinese twin requirements as checks: CIM layering, fire clearances (GB 50016), graded LOD, and the Q0-Q5 gates a delivery must pass.

skills.name: twin-workshop
skills.summary: The workshop scene class: equipment/workstation/production-line elements, LOD3-4 precision, indoor/maintainable parts and the highest Q4 fidelity bar.

skills.name: twin-city
skills.summary: The city-district scene class: LOD1-2 breadth-over-precision, 3D Tiles streaming from the same IR, and georeferencing as a hard Q3 gate.

skills.name: twin-plan
skills.summary: The harness plan: produce ParkProgram IR first (gen-ir), only then run the geometry operators; the run.prepare / finish hooks block the build until Q1 self-consistency passes. The loop for a new twin scene.
